items.title: ELO
items.description: Platform developed during the Health and Technology Hackathon in November 2026, designed to connect real healthcare needs with an accessible digital experience.
items.longDescription: ELO was created collaboratively in November 2026 during a health and technology hackathon. The project combined rapid product ideation, understanding a real healthcare challenge, and structuring a functional platform within the competition timeframe.
items.problem: In healthcare environments, information tracking and communication are often fragmented, calling for clearer and more approachable digital tools.
items.objective: Design and structure, within the intensive timeframe of a hackathon, a platform focused on usability, clear user flows, and practical healthcare application.
items.solution: Collaborative development of the ELO platform, organizing the user journey into an intuitive interface focused on healthcare connection and support.
process: Immersion into the healthcare hackathon challenge and definition of the core scope.
Collaborative structuring of user navigation flows and platform interface.
Consolidation and presentation of the functional and technical proposal.
features: Conceived around real healthcare and technology challenges.
Interface crafted for clarity, accessibility, and ease of use.
Team collaboration bridging product thinking and software development.

items.title: Laboratory Scheduling System
items.description: Practical application built to organize and manage laboratory reservations, time slots, and room availability.
items.longDescription: The Laboratory Scheduling System was developed to address the practical need of coordinating shared laboratory spaces and schedules, preventing booking conflicts and making availability easy to inspect.
items.metrics: Practical application for schedule & room management
items.problem: Manual or decentralized laboratory tracking often leads to overlapping bookings and makes it difficult to quickly check which rooms are available.
items.objective: Create a structured system for checking time slots, registering reservation requests, and clearly visualizing laboratory occupancy.
items.solution: Implementation of an application organized by laboratory spaces and time intervals, enabling clear tracking and management of reservations.
process: Mapped core reservation rules, time slots, and laboratory identifiers.
Modeled room information, available periods, and booking records.
Built a clean interface for quick availability lookup and reservation handling.
features: Structured availability view by laboratory and time slot.
Clear workflow for creating and organizing room bookings.
Clean interface tailored to academic routines.

items.title: Educational Quiz Game — Show do Milhão
items.description: Interactive question-and-answer educational game inspired by 'Show do Milhão', combining programming logic with dynamic learning.
items.longDescription: Hands-on project applying programming logic, state control, and event handling to build a complete educational quiz game inspired by the classic 'Show do Milhão' format.
items.problem: Traditional study review formats can feel static; gamified mechanics boost engagement and help reinforce knowledge.
items.objective: Develop a functional question-and-answer game with progressive rounds, answer validation, and mechanics inspired by 'Show do Milhão'.
items.solution: Built the question selection logic, level-based score progression, match lifelines/aids, and immediate visual feedback for each answer.
process: Structured the question bank, answer options, and difficulty progression.
Implemented scoring rules, answer verification, and in-game help mechanics.
Created the interactive interface guiding players across rounds.
features: Lifeline and scoring mechanics inspired by the Show do Milhão format.
Immediate visual feedback for right answers, mistakes, and level progression.
Practical application of decision structures and state management.

items.title: Velore
items.description: Personal financial assistant project currently in development, designed to simplify tracking and organizing personal finances.
items.longDescription: Velore is an active personal project combining my studies in software development and artificial intelligence to create a personal financial assistant focused on clarity and everyday organization.
items.problem: Tracking expenses, organizing categories, and maintaining visibility over personal finances often requires complex spreadsheets or cluttered apps.
items.objective: Progressively build a personal financial assistant capable of organizing financial information and providing a clearer, smarter tracking experience.
items.solution: Continuously evolving architecture prioritizing a clean software foundation, structured financial organization, and gradual integration of intelligent assistant capabilities.
process: Defined product vision, initial scope, and foundational application architecture.
Iterative development of system structure and core workflows (ongoing).
Research and experimentation with intelligent assistant capabilities for personal finance.
features: Personal project currently in active development.
Focused on personal financial organization with a streamlined user experience.
Practical laboratory for applying software engineering and artificial intelligence.
Continuous evolution of architecture and features.

about.title: Far beyond code.
about.lead: I'm Lucas Cecareli Ribeiro, a Computer Science student at Instituto Mauá de Tecnologia. I enjoy turning ideas into real projects, exploring software development, web applications, and artificial intelligence.
about.storyParagraph1: I believe learning technology goes beyond theory. It means experimenting, building, facing challenges, and evolving with every project.
about.storyParagraph2: Throughout my degree at Instituto Mauá de Tecnologia (2025–2029), I put this mindset into practice across academic software projects, the Health & Technology Hackathon with the ELO platform, and the ongoing development of Velore.

whyTech.title: Why I Chose Technology
whyTech.body: Computer science brings together logical reasoning, creativity, and direct impact. What motivates me most is taking a concrete idea or problem and building, line by line, an application that organizes workflows, teaches, or makes everyday tasks simpler.

interests.title: Software Development & AI
interests.body: My primary interests lie in software development, modern web applications, and Artificial Intelligence — learning how to combine clean code practices with increasingly intelligent systems.

goals.title: Professional Goals
goals.body: I aim to continuously strengthen my technical foundation throughout my degree at Mauá, take on challenging projects, and pursue internship and practical opportunities where I can contribute, learn from experienced teams, and grow as a developer.
